programs.title: AskDoc.X Health Systems Literacy for Healthcare Workers
outcomes: Explain how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO structures decisions and which actions stay human-reserved
Summarize evidence on AI-assisted healthcare using the Research Synthesis Lab's monitoring workflow
Draft a workplace question or proposal for the Proposal Forum using agent-drafted, human-decided process

sessions.activity: Tour the charter: mission, contribution model and measurable outcomes; map the six human-reserved governance actions and discuss why they stay with people.
Practice reading an Evidence Monitor summary and a Research Synthesis Agent brief; compare against a Mayo-area care workflow question raised by members.
Small groups turn a workplace concern into a proposal outline; the Proposal & Grant Drafter agent shapes it, members debate and simulate a human-only final vote.
Review Progress Tracker outputs against charter outcomes; members identify which metrics matter for frontline healthcare work and log follow-ups.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized pre/post quiz scores and proposal-topic categories (no member names or employer identifiers) to help improve synthesis-brief clarity for worker audiences.
programs.consent: Union-side orientation explains data use; members opt in individually and may contribute scores anonymously or decline data sharing while fully participating.

programs.title: AskDoc.X: Who Decides? A Civics of AI Field Study
outcomes: Describe Rochester's Mayo Clinic and Zumbro River setting and why expert knowledge concentrates there
Identify the difference between agent tasks and human-reserved decisions in a DAO
Collaborate on a simple, evidence-based proposal and vote as a class

sessions.activity: Explore the mission of governing AI as a public good; students sort sample decisions into 'agent does' vs 'humans only' buckets.
Act as junior Evidence Monitors: read a short, kid-friendly summary about AI in medicine and list two facts and one open question.
Groups draft a class proposal to improve school health communication; a drafter agent helps refine wording, then every student casts a final vote.
Students record their proposal's outcome on a simple progress chart and reflect on how measurable outcomes keep projects honest.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized class-level tallies of sorted-decision answers and proposal votes (no individual student names or work samples).
programs.consent: Guardian/parent consent forms and school approval obtained before the unit; only aggregate, anonymous class data is shared, and parents may opt out of any data contribution.

programs.title: Governance-by-Design: Running Human-Decided Programs Alongside Agents
outcomes: Design a program workflow that routes agent tasks to humans at decision points
Apply evidence-synthesis practices to a health-equity or community-health question
Structure measurable outcomes aligned with a public-good charter

sessions.activity: Map a real NGO program onto task-routing: what a Task Router and Collaborator Scout could support, and where staff judgment is mandatory.
Build an evidence table on a community-health question using the monitoring-to-synthesis pipeline practiced in the lab zone.
Teams draft a grant-style proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter; peers debate; staff simulate the human-only enact step and note reserved actions.
Define 2-3 measurable outcomes for the drafted program and set up a tracking template mirroring the Progress Tracker.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized workflow maps and outcome-metric templates (organization names removed) to a shared library of governance-by-design patterns.
programs.consent: Participating organizations sign a data-sharing addendum; any client or beneficiary data stays out of scope, and submissions are scrubbed of identifiers before sharing.

programs.title: Charter to Impact: A Nonprofit Board Workshop on Human-Governed AI
outcomes: Explain the agent-managed, human-governed model and the six human-reserved actions to a board audience
Assess which nonprofit decisions can be agent-supported and which must remain board-reserved
Adopt a simple charter-aligned outcomes dashboard

sessions.activity: Board walkthrough of the charter, contribution model and measurable outcomes; compare with the nonprofit's own bylaws and reserved powers.
Directors practice the proposal lifecycle: agent drafts, board debates, humans alone vote to enact; apply to one live nonprofit decision.
Identify which staff tasks could be agent-assisted versus board-governed; sketch a routing policy with clear human checkpoints.
Build a one-page outcomes dashboard modeled on the Progress Tracker; agree on review cadence and who sees it.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized governance-pattern summaries (which decision types boards reserve, cadence choices) with identifiers removed, to a shared governance-pattern library.
programs.consent: Board resolution authorizes participation; individual directors consent to workshop participation, and only de-identified governance patterns are shared externally.
